title: Praise for the Faithful Creator
overview: This psalm calls people to joyful praise because God made the world by his word, outlasts human plans, sees everyone, and protects those who hope in his steady love.

parts.label: A call to joyful music (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The singer invites people who try to live rightly to praise God with harp and ten-stringed lyre, playing well and loudly. A "new song" most likely means fresh praise fitted to a new occasion or a new reason for thanks.

parts.label: Reliable and kind (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: The first reason for praise is that God's word can be trusted, his actions are faithful, and he cares about fairness and justice. The Hebrew word for his love means loyal, steady kindness, and the psalm says the whole earth is full of it.

parts.label: A world made by speaking (vv. 6-9)
parts.note: God simply speaks, and the sky, the stars and the seas take shape and hold firm, echoing the creation story in Genesis 1. Christians have read the "word" and "breath" here as hinting at Jesus and the Holy Spirit, though the psalm itself does not spell that out.

parts.label: Plans that last (vv. 10-15)
parts.note: The schemes of nations fall apart, but God's purposes last through every generation, and Israel counts itself fortunate to be the people he chose as his own. Yet he watches every person on earth, and because he shaped every heart, he understands what drives what people do.

parts.label: False hopes and true hope (vv. 16-19)
parts.note: Big armies, strong warriors and war horses, the greatest powers of the ancient world, are called a false hope that cannot truly save. Instead, God keeps watch over those who trust his love, to rescue them from death and keep them alive when famine comes.

parts.label: Waiting together (vv. 20-22)
parts.note: The psalm ends with the whole community speaking as one, waiting on God as their help and shield. They ask that his steady love rest on them, in the same measure as they put their hope in him.

think: What do you tend to lean on to feel safe, and how well has it held up when things got hard?
